description:
Hi! I'm a React developer working on the Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge. I'm building "FireScope" — an interactive web app visualizing global fire seasons using NASA data. I will handle the frontend architecture, API integration, and map design.

I'm looking for teammates into Earth Science, Data Analysis, or UI/UX Design to help process data or polish the interface. Let's collaborate!
summary:
BurnCal is an interactive web application designed to solve the 2026 NASA challenge: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots. By merging fragmented satellite datasets into a unified burning activity calendar, it provides a seamless and accessible geospatial dashboard.

Users can explore an interactive 3D globe, select specific countries, and apply advanced filters (confidence, Fire Radiative Power, time of day) to analyze historical fire patterns and critical periods.

To deliver actionable intelligence, BurnCal calculates estimated CO₂ emissions and a custom Fire Severity Index. It also features a proximity alert system that notifies users of sustained, high-intensity fires within a 75 km radius of their saved location. By transforming raw satellite data into intuitive visualizations and exportable formats (Excel, GeoJSON), BurnCal empowers environmental analysts, researchers, and general users to quickly assess ecological damage and track seasonal fire trends.
details:
How it works & What it does:
BurnCal is a React-based web application that harmonizes active fire hotspot data from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS sensors into a unified "burning activity calendar." Users can navigate an interactive 2D/3D globe, select any country, and load near real-time satellite data. The app features advanced geospatial filtering, allowing users to isolate fires by confidence level, Fire Radiative Power (FRP), and time of day (to study diurnal patterns). Data is visualized through dynamic charts (showing fire counts or total intensity) and a heatmap mode for density clustering.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
The project solves the problem of data fragmentation. By merging disparate satellite datasets, it provides a unified, accessible view for environmental analysts, researchers, and general users. To deliver actionable intelligence, BurnCal calculates estimated CO₂ emissions and a custom Fire Severity Index (0-100). The intended impact is data democratization: transforming complex CSV files into intuitive visualizations and one-click exports (Excel, GeoJSON).

The Alert System (Addressing Data Delay):
Because NASA FIRMS data has a processing delay, BurnCal's alert system is specifically designed to flag sustained, extreme fire events (FRP > 100 MW) within a 75 km radius of a user's saved location. By filtering out small, transient fires, the system ensures users only receive alerts for large, ongoing situations that represent a genuine threat.

Tools & Tech Stack:
Built using React, Vite, and JavaScript. Key libraries include @cublya/geomap (for 3D globe rendering), recharts (for data visualization), and d3-geo & @turf/bbox (for strict geospatial filtering). External APIs include NASA FIRMS (fire data), Photon (city autocomplete), and Nominatim (reverse geocoding). Data is exported using xlsx.

Creativity & Factors Considered:
A major creative factor was handling strict spatial accuracy. I used d3-geo and @turf/bbox to ensure fires are plotted strictly within a country's borders, successfully solving the complex geometry problem of the 180th meridian. I also implemented smart caching to save API bandwidth and URL state management, allowing users to share their exact map view and filters.

Note: AI tools (LLMs) were used for coding assistance, debugging, and drafting documentation. The core logic, ideation, spatial filtering, and application architecture were designed and implemented by the author.
